title: Sentinel KV + Prefix Cache Handoff — Weekly POC Sync
summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on KV/prefix cache hit-rate trends, prompt-reuse patterns, and a handoff plan for telemetry dashboards. Action items assigned for dashboard export, profiling run, and security doc share.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Chen (Sentinel ML Eng), Maya Alvarez (PM), Jonas Becker (Data Eng)

Auto-summary: Weekly sync to review KV/prefix cache hit-rate, discuss prompt reuse patterns seen in the pilot, and finalize handoff steps for telemetry and tuning. Conversation included specific tuning proposals and an agreement to run an A/B prefetch test.

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's try to keep to 45 minutes, agenda: hit-rate numbers, prompt reuse, tuning proposals, then next steps. Riley, Maya, you good with that?
[00:18] Riley (Sentinel): Yeah that works. Quick note, there's a stakeholder in EMEA so I might need to drop around 15:25 UTC but I'll stay as long as I can.
[00:26] Samir (Redwood SE): Cool. I'll start with a quick recap of where the KV/prefix hit-rate landed after last week's eviction threshold tweak.
[00:36] Samir: So, high level — overall KV hit-rate moved from about 21% to 32% across the conversational cohort, prefix-only hit-rate up modestly, maybe 6 points. Important: hit distribution is skewed, the top 12% of sessions account for ~68% of hits, long-tail is basically zero.
[01:02] Riley: Hmm, that matches our internal logs. A lot of the clinical question flows repeat identical prompts for common templates, but we get a big tail of ad-hoc clinician queries.
[01:14] Ava: Right, so we have two levers: increase prefix TTL to capture more convo reuse, and tighten eviction for the very low frequency keys. Samir, your recommendation?
[01:24] Samir: I propose a hybrid: bump prefix TTL from 15s to 90s for conversational routes where session length > 3 turns, and apply a frequency-based eviction alpha for KV entries that haven't been hit in X hours. Also enable a cheap prefetch for predicted next-token prefixes for top 10 intents.
[01:46] Jonas (Sentinel): When you say prefetch, do you mean materializing KV entries proactively or warming the model cache? We're worried about costs if we start prefetching aggressively.
[01:55] Samir: Good clarif — prefetch here is KV prefetch: query the DB/cache to warm the prefix set so the first lookups hit locally. Not spinning extra GPU work. Cost impact is minimal compared to model token costs.
[02:12] Maya: But isn't there a cost to storage/IO if we prefetch a lot? Our infra team is sensitive to that.
[02:18] Samir: Yes, which is why the hybrid runs only for top predicted intents and uses a TTL, plus we cap prefetch QPS. We suggested a 48hr A/B where half the traffic uses current policy, half uses hybrid prefetch.
[02:34] Riley: Ok that A/B sounds reasonable. How big a sample do you need?
[02:37] Samir: For statistical power on hit-rate and latency tradeoffs, ~2M requests over 48 hours should give a clear signal given your volume — but we can scope to a percentage if you want to limit the run.
[02:47] Jonas: We can do 20% of production traffic routed to the A/B.
[02:51] Ava: Great. Next, prompt reuse patterns — Riley, you mentioned you saw prompt normalization doing weird splits?
[02:58] Riley: Yeah the tokenizer normalization in our trace munging seems to be splitting clinical abbreviations, so we undercount reuse. For example, "BP" becomes "b p" sometimes, so the prefix key differs.
[03:12] Samir: Classic tokenization artifact. We recommend running a normalization pass upstream to canonicalize common clinic tokens before generating prefix keys. Also include a fuzzy-match for punctuation variants.
[03:24] Riley: I'll add that to the preprocessing pipeline. Could that affect semantic matching and cause false positives?
[03:29] Samir: It can — we should only canonicalize safe abbreviations and keep a rollback. We'll provide a recommended whitelist.
[03:36] Maya: Any thoughts on metrics? What should we watch beyond raw KV hit-rate?
[03:41] Samir: Good question. Watch: cold-start latency, p50/p95 token latencies, model token cost per session, and prefix reuse ratio. Also track cross-session contamination risk — i.e., ensure RBAC and tenant isolation metrics stay clean.
[03:56] Jonas: On tenant isolation — do we need to worry about shared caches leaking identifiers?
[03:59] Ava: We already scoped tenant tagging in the POC; Redwood's prefix cache is namespaced by tenant id, but we'll surface the audit logs for you.
[04:09] Riley: Speaking of audit logs, can you export the KV hit-rate dashboard raw CSV? Our analytics team wants to join with event logs.
[04:16] Ava: Yes we'll export it after the call. Samir, can you bundle the raw query samples too?
[04:20] Samir: Yep, I'll include a small sampling and the sampling script.
[04:24] [05:00] (brief silence as people check notes)
[05:12] Maya: We also ran into an odd eviction spike at 03:00 UTC on Monday where TTLs were being shortened — not sure if that's due to autoscaler churn
[05:22] Samir: Autoscaler churn can cause eviction if nodes are rebalanced; we have heuristics to pin hot shards. I'll check logs and correlate with your timeline.
[05:30] Jonas: If it's autoscaler-caused, can we change the eviction fallback to be more conservative during scale events?
[05:36] Samir: Yes, we can soften eviction during detected rebalance windows — add a grace factor. That'll reduce churn but slightly increase memory use.
[05:44] Riley: Acceptable tradeoff.
[05:47] Ava: Let's talk about telemetry handoff — we propose a dashboard export + a short handoff doc for your ops team. Who will own that on Sentinel?
[05:55] Maya: Jonas will take ops ownership and coordinate with analytics. Jonas?
[06:00] Jonas: Yep I'll own it. I need the CSV and the sampling script.
[06:06] Samir: I'll attach the script and a README, small Python runbook for staging.
[06:11] Riley: On the topic of security, our compliance lead wants to confirm KMS support for the private deployment variant. Are we still good there?
[06:19] Ava: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; Samir can share the security checklist.
[06:25] Samir: I'll paste the SOC2 scoping doc, and the KMS integration notes.
[06:29] Maya: Great. Also one question about fallback models — if a KV miss occurs we currently fall back to a larger model which increases latency. Any strategy to reduce this tail?
[06:39] Samir: Two approaches: increase hit-rate (prefix TTL + prefetch) or route misses to a cheaper yet slightly larger model variant than your small one, i.e., a mid-tier model to avoid the full big-model cost. We can also use a short timeout and return cached partial responses.
[06:55] Riley: We prefer the mid-tier fallback. Can Redwood recommend a model variant?
[07:00] Samir: We'll share model profiles comparing lat/throughput/cost for the fallback options.
[07:06] Ava: Ok next up — specific tuning plan for the week. Samir?
[07:11] Samir: Actionable plan: (1) Export current prefix/KV hit distribution (Ava will share CSV). (2) Samir runs staging profiling with whitelist normalization and posts results. (3) Jonas provides long-tail query set for eviction tuning. (4) Launch 48hr 20% A/B hybrid prefetch on 2027-06-07. We'll measure hit-rate delta and p95 latency.
[07:33] Maya: Sounds good. One more ask: can Redwood annotate samples where reuse was blocked by tokenization so we can update our upstream normalizer?
[07:41] Samir: Yes, we'll mark a sample set and include diff highlights.
[07:45] Riley: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:48] Ava: No major blockers; just need access to the staging logs and permission to run the profiling script. Jonas, can you grant Samir staging read access?
[07:55] Jonas: I'll open a ticket after the call and cc Samir.
[07:59] Ava: Perfect. Anything else?
[08:02] (small cross chatter)
[08:10] Maya: Timeline recap? I have to create an internal summary for execs.
[08:15] Ava: Sure — we'll send a one-pager: recommended tuning changes, A/B plan, timelines, and action items. Expect that by EOD 2027-06-03.
[08:25] Riley: EOD is great.
[08:28] Samir: I'll also drop the profiling script and readme into the shared folder.
[08:32] Jonas: And I'll open the staging access ticket.
[08:36] Ava: Ok let's close with the explicit next steps — quick readout so everyone leaves aligned.
[08:42] (round-robin confirmation)
[09:00] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the CSV and the one-pager.

End transcript.

Notes on transcript quality and artifacts: occasional tokenization names were mis-transcribed as "kay-vee" or "K V"; some proper nouns (e.g., stakeholder names) may be slightly off. Shared artifacts: link: /shared/sentinel/poc/hitrate-dashboard (Redwood console), link: /shared/sentinel/poc/profiling-script.py (Samir's script) — links to be shared in follow-up email.
